heading: Targets
body: The bundle targets are web, macos, windows, linux, ios and android. The web target writes browser assets. Every other target prepares a host that contains the platform WebView. Native packaging needs the SDKs (software development kits) and host tools for that platform. The windows target also needs the WebView2 SDK: restore the `Microsoft.Web.WebView2` package and set `TAC_WEBVIEW2_SDK` to the folder where you extracted it, or the build stops with `TY1605`. Build a Windows app on Windows, from a Visual Studio developer prompt, so that `cl` and the Windows SDK are on the PATH. `--arch x64` or `--arch arm64` chooses the app's architecture. Without `--arch`, an ARM64 build machine builds an ARM64 app and other machines build an x64 app. Open the prompt that matches: on a Windows on Arm PC, `vcvarsall.bat arm64` for an ARM64 app or `vcvarsall.bat arm64_amd64` for an x64 app. A prompt for the other architecture stops the build with `TY1605`. A Windows app shows its page only in a signed-in desktop session. Started from a service or an SSH session, the window opens but WebView2 cannot attach to it, so the page stays empty. The all target builds every target. It writes one folder for each target under dist/. You must still test on each platform.
